findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the heat sanitizing dish machine to reach a dish plate temperature of 150-154F after running several cycles. Inspector discussed proper heat sanitizing temperatures with the person in charge (PIC). The facility has been directed to utilize the triple sink for chemical sanitation until the machine’s heat boosters have been adjusted to reach a minimum plate temperature of 158F (FDA food codes allows for +/-2 instrument error). Inform the inspector if the machine has been adjusted prior to the follow up date.
findings.citation_text: 4-703.11(B) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (B) Hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through EQUIPMENT that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a UTENSIL surface temperature of 71°C (160°F) as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: A sanitizer bucket on the prep counter was observed with no measurable sanitizer concentration. CORRECTED- Sanitizer buckets were emptied and remade at the 3 compartment sink wall-mounted dispenser. Sanitizer buckets were then observed at 400ppm quat. Ensure sanitizer buckets are remade periodically.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114 (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling (200-400ppm). [P]

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The kitchen restroom door is not self-closing. Add a self-closer to the restroom door.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.14 A toilet room located on the PREMISES shall be completely enclosed and provided with a tight-fitting and self-closing door. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Sanitizer spray bottles observed with no measurable quat sanitizer concentration. CORRECTED- Sanitizer concentrate jug was replaced and spray bottles were remade. Sanitizer was observed at 200 ppm.
4-501.114: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have a concentration based on the label (200-400ppm). [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Caulk is not sealing the edge of the dish area drainboards to the wall. Reseal drainboards to the wall. 
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Raw shell eggs observed stored over ready-to-eat foods (shredded cheese, tortillas, etc) in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- Storage rearranged to prevent potential cross contamination. Discussed storing eggs below ready-to-eat food.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
Facility does not have a vomit/diarrhea clean up policy available on file. CORRECTED- Inspector provided a printed copy of a vomit/diarrhea clean up policy to be posted or kept on file.
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  [Pf]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Spray bottles used for quat sanitizer were empty at the start of inspection. Breakfast service recently ended and lunch prep was underway. Solutions at proper concentration were provided during inspection. Ensure quat solutions are prepared and available for use during all hours of prep and operation.
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Upon arrival a member of the kitchen staff was observed adjusting their face mask and did not wash hands prior to continuing with their next task. Handwashing between tasks and after adjustment of face mask were discussed. Employee was observed washing hands between tasks as needed for remainder of inspection. Ensure proper handwashing between tasks. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands should also be washed after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.13 Irreversible registering temperature indicator was not available for checking the final rinse surface temperature at the dishes during a ware washing cycle. Options for dish machine temperature test strips and maximum registering thermometers were discussed.
In hot water mechanical warewashing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature. Surface temperature at dishes upon completion of final rinse must be at least 160F for proper heat sanitization.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 After making a phone call an employee returned to the prep area and got a pair of gloves to finish prep without first washing hands. Hand washing between tasks and glove changes were discussed. Hands were washed prior to putting gloves to continue with salad bar prep.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands should also be washed prior to donning gloves/between glove changes, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15(A) Employee adjusted face mask with gloved hands while doing salad bar prep and did not immediately remove gloves for disposal. Proper glove use was discussed. Ensure gloves are changed between tasks/as needed and any time gloved hands touch general surfaces unrelated to food prep/handling.
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Food employees were observed entering/exiting the walkin cooler and changing gloves without consistent handwashing in between. Discussed washing hands between tasks and glove changes. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands should also be washed prior to donning gloves/between glove changes, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Gloves used properly
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15 Food employee did not change gloves after touching the faucet of the prep sink to rinse a cutting board during vegetable prep. Employee continued wearing the same gloves to continue handling vegetables. Proper glove use was discussed. Gloves were discarded prior to employee getting a fresh pair of gloves to continue with food prep. Handwashing between glove changes was also discussed.
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Paper towels were not present at the restroom handsink. Paper towels were stocked in the dispenser, and a spare roll was provided by custodial staff. 
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with Individual, disposable towels or another approved drying option.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) - Can opener blade was soiled with buildup from use on a prior operating day. Can opener was cleaned and sanitized in the dish machine during the inspection.

Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch.  Wash, rinse, and sanitize the can opener between uses.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-803.11 - Used/soiled wiping cloth from the previous day's operation was observed on the divider of the prep sink basins. Per the manager, soiled wiping cloths are to be dried in the designated area by the back door prior to taking linens to the elementary school for laundering. Wiping cloth was placed in the proper storage area. 

Soiled linens must be stored in a cleanable container in an area to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) - Top of knife storage rack was beginning to accumulate dust and debris. Cleaning frequency was discussed. Manager cleaned the knife storage rack during the inspection. 

Clean equipment and utensils shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; and 4) covered or inverted.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12(A) - Floor in the dish area was soiled with general buildup along the wall juncture an under the booster heater. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 

Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-305.11(B)-An employee jacket was observed hanging on dry storage shelving. Jacket was placed in proper storage area. An employee was later observed placing her coat on the same set of shelving. Manager discussed proper storage of personal items with staff, and all personal items were placed in the proper storage area. 

Food establishments shall provide lockers or other suitable facilities for the orderly storage of employees' clothing and other possessions.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.citation_text:
750.830 - Labels on pans of deli sandwiches in the walkin cooler had a date mark of 1/22. Sandwiches were just prepared this morning. Any leftover deli meat used today would have been opened as of 1/23. Staff were advised on date marking and that labels are not required if products will be used within a 24hr time frame. Leftover portions in original packaging need labels, but lids for same day use would not require labeling. If labels are used, then make sure labels are removed daily to allow for proper cleaning and sanitizing of all surfaces during ware washing process.

Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dishwashing machine unless a pre-wash cycle is a part of the dishwashing machine operation.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Employee that just arrived to work pulled a bag of lettuce from the walkin cooler and retrieved a cutting board to begin prep prior to washing hands. Employee was observed washing hands prior to beginning food handling but was advised to wash hands upon entering the kitchen and before handling clean equipment as well.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated, upon entering the kitchen to begin work, before putting gloves/between glove changes, and before working with food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - Dry storage food shelves were soiled with oil accumulation. It appeared a cooking oil bottle may have been damaged at some point.
Also, the lower shelf in dry storage (bottom of spice storage shelving) was observed with some old mouse droppings.
Clean the dry storage shelves, and sanitize the area where droppings were observed.

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1200 & 1220 - Floors were soiled in the following areas:
A) dish area - 1. under booster heater (moisture/debris) & 2. far right corner (old mouse droppings);
B) dry storage - 1. under cooking oil storage (spilled oil) & 2. along walls and in corners, especially under spice storage, around the safe, the transformer, and the manager's desk (old mouse droppings).
Clean the floors in the aforementioned areas.
NOTE: Custodial staff caught a mouse ~3 months ago, and staff have not observed any apparent activity recently.  Droppings appeared to be from old activity. Management noted a detail cleaning will be conducted.

Significant gap was observed at the floor to wall juncture of the back wall in the dry storage room. Seal and repair the floor.

Floors must be in good repair, constructed to facilitate easy cleaning, and maintained clean.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - Sani-bucket used by custodial staff to wipe down tables was registering at 0ppm quat. Manager noted it was prepared earlier that morning. Another bucket was prepared and still tested at 0ppm quat. The chemical was allowed to flow from the wall mounted dispenser for a few minutes and was still observed at 0ppm. Sani-Tabs were available for preparing sanitizer solutions. A new bucket was prepared. Sanitizer spray bottles were observed at 0ppm and were also remade. New solutions were observed at 200-400ppm quat (as per approved range on the directions of bottle). Use test strips to verify sanitizer is maintained at proper concentration, and change solutions as needed (every 2-4hrs for bucket; or more often if solutions and wiping cloths become heavily soiled).
Until the wall mounted sanitizer dispenser is fixed Sani-Tabs will be utilized for preparing quat solutions. Manager noted a call for service would be made to GFS to get the chemical dispenser repaired.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - A) Debris was observed on the edge of the can opener blade. Can opener had not been used yet in daily operations. Can opener was placed through dish machine during inspection.

B) Accumulation of old food debris was observed along the clean in place portion of the slicer. Manager noted the slicer was last used the week prior. Proper manual wash, rinse, and sanitize of clean in place part of the slicer was discussed. The slicer will be thoroughly cleaned and sanitized prior to next use.

To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use. In-use equipment must be cleaned and sanitized up to every 4hrs after continuous use. For those items that can not be placed in the dish machine for ware washing (i.e. base of slicer), proper manual wash, rinse, and sanitize must occur for the food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Foods properly cooked and/or reheated
findings.comment:
750180 & 210 - Refried beans and taco meat were observed in the warming cabinet; internal temperatures were 108F-113F and 133F-135F respectively. Taco meat was a reheat (cooked on 2/1) and beans were reconstituted this morning. Items were placed in the warming cabinet for temporary storage until the steamer was available. Staff were advised all foods must be cooked/reheated to proper temperatures prior to being placed in hot holding units. Beans and taco meat were placed in the oven to finish properly heating foods.

Potentially hazardous foods shall be reheated rapidly to 165F/higher throughout the product. All potentially hazardous foods shall be cooked to the proper product temperature. (see general comments)

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - Soap was not available at kitchen handsink upon arrival of inspector. Soap was provided during the inspection.

Maintain an adequate supply of soap and paper towels at handsinks to allow for proper handwashing.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-151(a) Observed bulk American cheese in a plastic bag marked 2/2. Discussed storage practices with employee who insisted the cheese was pulled from the freezer after the 2/2 date. Make sure that the movement of potentially hazardous foods is properly documented as it moves through the kitchen. Discussed proliferation of Lysteria in foods held longer than seven days at 41F or below. Keep track of foods as they move from fridge to freezer and back to fridge. Freezer stops the seven day countdown and so days foods are kept frozen must be tracked. Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 750-130f Observed bulk container of sugar to not be labeled with common name. Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750-160  Observed the stem thermometer stored on the counter to be soiled with dried, old food debris. During the inspection, the thermometer was pulled for cleaning and sanitizing - CORRECTED. Make sure that stem thermometers are washed/sanitized before being placed in storage.  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.comment: 750-160 Observed a cup being used as a scoop in the bulk sugar container. Pulled from use during inspection  - CORRECTED.  Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact.
